private.summary: Regulation applies to law enforcement agencies only. No ALPR-specific obligations apply to private operators.

le.summary: Permitted for criminal justice and public safety purposes only. Data cannot be sold. Access log and dissemination log required for all uses and transfers.
le.retention: 5 years maximum. Data tied to an active investigation may be retained beyond 5 years.
le.data_sharing: Criminal justice agencies only, for criminal justice or public safety purposes.
notable_points: Written policy required.
Annual report required.
Audit required.

private.summary: Permitted for property owners, leaseholders, and commercial businesses for security and access control only. Any other private use is unlawful.
private.data_sharing: Only with contracted asset protection analytics services. Contract must prohibit other uses and cap retention at 60 days.

pra.notes: Yes — actual damages or $1,000 per violation, whichever is higher, plus costs.

notable_points: Selling ALPR data is prohibited.
Semiannual statistical report required — must be available to the Legislature on request.

le.summary: LE use permitted.
le.retention: Not specified.
le.data_sharing: Not specified.

pra.notes: Yes — actual damages or $1,000 per violation, whichever is higher, plus costs.

meta.new_statute_note: Act 668 (April 2025) significantly expanded private use rights — prior law effectively forbade all private use.

private.summary: Legal review required before deployment. Whether a private entity qualifies as an 'operator' under state law is unsettled and actively litigated — that classification determines key compliance obligations.
private.data_sharing: No ALPR-specific cross-border restriction on private operators. General privacy law applies.

pra.notes: Yes — $2,500 minimum per violation. Private citizens can sue directly. Punitive damages possible for willful violations.

notable_points: Operators must post a public ALPR usage policy and complete a training program before deployment.
The operator classification question is being actively litigated in Javorsky and Eldridge.
litigation: AG Bonta sued the City of El Cajon (Oct. 2025) for sharing ALPR data with out-of-state agencies — first enforcement action under California's ALPR statute. Applies to public agencies.

Javorsky v. Flock Safety (filed Feb. 26, 2026, SF Superior Court) — class action against Flock directly for enabling cross-state data sharing. SFPD cameras were accessed by out-of-state agencies over 1.6 million times.
Eldridge v. Flock Group Inc. (filed March 2026) — second class action against Flock over data sharing violations.

le.summary: Data cannot leave California. This restriction applies to agencies and their contracted vendors. Each violation carries a $2,500 minimum penalty. Private citizens can sue directly.
le.retention: No specified limit.
le.data_sharing: Within California only. No out-of-state or federal sharing under any circumstances.

pra.notes: Yes — $2,500 minimum per violation. Private citizens can sue directly. Same exposure applies to contracted vendors.

litigation: AG Bonta sued the City of El Cajon (Oct. 2025) for sharing ALPR data with out-of-state agencies — first enforcement action under California's ALPR statute.

Javorsky v. Flock Safety (filed Feb. 26, 2026, SF Superior Court) — class action against Flock for enabling cross-state data sharing. SFPD cameras were accessed 1.6 million times by out-of-state agencies.
Eldridge v. Flock Group Inc. (filed March 2026) — second class action against Flock over data sharing violations.

private.summary: No ALPR-specific statute applies to private operators. General privacy law applies.

le.summary: No ALPR-specific statute. A general passive surveillance records law caps data retention at 3 years.
le.retention: 3 years maximum.
le.data_sharing: Exempt from public records disclosure.
notable_points: Access after year one is restricted to records linked to a filed claim or specific incident.

private.summary: A statute exists but is not yet effective — the DC Council passed it without appropriating funds to implement it. No legal effect until funded.

pra.notes: Not under ALPR law — statute is not yet effective.

notable_points: Statute exists but is unfunded and not yet operative. Could activate if DC appropriates funding.

le.summary: A statute exists but is not yet effective — the DC Council passed it without appropriating funds to implement it. No legal effect until funded.

pra.notes: Not under ALPR law — statute is not yet effective.

notable_points: Statute exists but is unfunded and not yet operative. Could activate if DC appropriates funding.

meta.watch_note: Statute passed but not funded — no legal effect yet. Could activate quickly if DC appropriates funding.

private.summary: Private use permitted.

le.summary: ALPR data is confidential and FOIA-exempt. Data may only be shared with other criminal justice agencies for official duties, or disclosed to the registered plate owner.
le.retention: 30 days for tactical use. Up to 3 years for active criminal investigations.
le.data_sharing: Criminal justice agencies only, for official duties. Disclosure to registered plate owner permitted.
notable_points: Retention schedule established by the Department of State in consultation with FDLE — not fixed in statute.
Installation on state highway right-of-way requires FDOT permit.

private.summary: Private use permitted. Knowingly misusing data is a criminal offense.

le.summary: Data may only be accessed for law enforcement purposes and must be destroyed within 30 months. Contractors are subject to the same policies and criminal liability as the agency.
le.retention: 30 months maximum.
le.data_sharing: Other LE agencies for law enforcement purposes. Contractors subject to agency policy.
notable_points: Written policy required covering training of law enforcement officers.
ALPR data is FOIA-exempt.
Misuse is a criminal offense.

private.summary: Statute applies to government agencies only. No ALPR-specific obligations apply to private operators.

le.summary: Permitted for felony and misdemeanor investigation, traffic accidents, and missing or endangered persons. No personal, political, or non-investigative surveillance use. Access restricted to authorized personnel.
le.retention: Not specified.
le.data_sharing: Access limited to authorized personnel only. Access controls required.
notable_points: Mandatory training required for all authorized users covering data privacy, legal compliance, and ethical use.
Every access must be logged: user identity, date, time, and purpose.
Semiannual audits of access logs required to detect unauthorized or suspicious activity.

private.summary: Private use permitted. ALPR data is exempt from FOIA disclosure.

le.summary: LE use permitted. ALPR data exempt from FOIA.
le.retention: Not specified.
le.data_sharing: Exempt from FOIA.

private.summary: No operational restrictions on private use. Statute creates a public records exemption only.
private.data_sharing: ALPR data exempt from public records disclosure.

le.summary: LE use permitted. Data protected from public disclosure.
le.retention: Not specified.
le.data_sharing: Exempt from public records requests.

private.summary: Private use is prohibited. No exceptions.

le.summary: Permitted for criminal investigations only. Data inputs must be based on documented facts of a safety concern or active investigation, or sourced from NCIC or an official law enforcement bulletin. Non-investigative data must be deleted within 21 days.
le.retention: 21 days for non-investigative reads. Investigative data retained for the case.
le.data_sharing: Law enforcement agencies only, for official functions, or in related civil or criminal proceedings. Aggregate summary reports may be released publicly.

private.summary: Private use permitted. No ALPR-specific obligations apply.

le.summary: Historical ALPR data may only be shared with the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC). Sharing with any other agency — including other Maryland agencies — is prohibited.
le.retention: Not specified.
le.data_sharing: MCAC only. All other sharing prohibited.
notable_points: Mandatory audits of ALPR systems required.
ALPR data is exempt from public records disclosure under Gen. Prov. § 4-326.

statute.citation: Md. Code, Pub. Safety § 3-509; Gen. Prov. § 4-326

private.summary: No ALPR-specific obligations apply to private operators. The statute addresses only private entities that voluntarily share data with a law enforcement agency — that data then becomes subject to LE restrictions.

le.summary: Non-investigative data must be destroyed within 60 days. Tracking an individual in an active criminal investigation requires a warrant or emergency circumstances. Data may only be matched against the Minnesota license plate file except in active investigations. No central state repository permitted.
le.retention: 60 days for non-investigative data.
le.data_sharing: Other LE agencies only, with same classification and destruction requirements. No selling, trading, or sharing with non-LE entities.
notable_points: Public log of ALPR use required, including active times, number of plates scanned, and fixed reader locations.
Independent biennial audit required; results are public. Commissioner of Administration can order suspension for noncompliance.
Role-based access controls and full audit trail of all queries and data actions required.
Bureau of Criminal Apprehension must be notified within 10 days of any installation.

private.summary: No ALPR-specific obligations apply to private operators.

le.summary: Data may only be used for law enforcement purposes and must be deleted within 90 days. Selling data is prohibited.
le.retention: 90 days maximum. Exceptions for preservation orders and search warrants.
le.data_sharing: Disclosure to other LE agencies for law enforcement purposes permitted. Exempt from public disclosure, except to the registered plate owner.
notable_points: Written policy required covering databases used, retention, sharing, training, supervisory oversight, and access controls.
Annual audit of use and effectiveness required, with findings reported to the agency head.
Data is classified as a public record but exempt from disclosure.

private.summary: Act applies to governmental entities only. No ALPR-specific obligations apply to private operators.

pra.notes: Yes — actual damages for anyone harmed by a violation. No minimum. Applies to businesses and individuals.

notable_points: Data obtained in violation cannot be used in court.

le.summary: Permitted for identifying: vehicles associated with missing persons, vehicles registered to someone with an outstanding warrant, vehicles relevant to an ongoing criminal investigation, stolen vehicles, and vehicles in violation of equipment or registration requirements. Parking enforcement agencies may use systems for parking and traffic violations, secured area enforcement, weigh stations, and toll collection.
le.retention: 60 days maximum. Exceptions for active evidence, preservation requests, warrants, subpoenas, and court orders.
le.data_sharing: Not a public record. Disclosed only to the registered owner, with the owner's consent, by court order, or as the result of a system match.

pra.notes: Yes — same damages as private track apply under § 60-3208.

notable_points: Annual reporting to Nebraska Crime Commission required.
Agencies must post a privacy policy.

private.summary: Private use is prohibited. No exceptions.

le.summary: Permitted for law enforcement only. Reads must be purged within 3 minutes in a manner that is destroyed and not recoverable. Data retained only where a read resulted in a hit — arrest, citation, protective custody, or identification of a missing person — in those cases, retained until end of case. A hit alone is not sufficient basis for a stop; officers must visually verify the plate before stopping.
le.retention: 3 minutes for reads. Retained until end of case if the read resulted in a hit (arrest, citation, protective custody, or missing person identification).
le.data_sharing: Not specified.
notable_points: LPR devices may not photograph or record vehicle occupants — plate only.
AG can seize devices for repeated violations.
Statute expires January 1, 2027. Monitor for replacement legislation.

meta.watch_note: Statute sunsets January 1, 2027. Monitor for replacement legislation.

private.summary: No ALPR-specific statute. General privacy and data law obligations still apply.

le.summary: No ALPR-specific statute. General privacy and data law obligations still apply.

private.summary: Private use permitted. Unlawful obtaining, accessing, or disclosing of data is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

le.summary: Data may only be used for law enforcement purposes. Traffic violation enforcement is prohibited. Data must be destroyed within 90 days.
le.retention: 90 days maximum. Exceptions for preservation orders and search warrants.
le.data_sharing: Criminal justice officers at LE agencies via written request for a legitimate LE purpose. No selling.
notable_points: Written policy required before system goes operational, covering databases, retention, sharing, training, supervisory oversight, access controls, and annual auditing.
Database updates required every 24 hours.
Maintenance and calibration records must be kept on file.
Violation is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

private.summary: Statute covers uninsured vehicle enforcement only. No other ALPR-specific law applies — general privacy obligations govern all other uses.

le.summary: No ALPR-specific restrictions apply to LE. The statute authorizes use for uninsured vehicle enforcement only. No retention, sharing, or policy requirements apply.
le.retention: Not specified.
le.data_sharing: Not specified.

private.summary: Statute applies to government agencies only. No ALPR-specific obligations apply to private operators.

le.summary: Data must be deleted within 90 days.
le.retention: 90 days maximum. Data tied to an active investigation retained until the case concludes, then deleted.
le.data_sharing: Not specified.

private.summary: Private use permitted. No ALPR-specific obligations apply.

le.summary: Permitted for specific purposes: active criminal investigations, outstanding warrants, missing persons, stolen vehicles, parking enforcement, and motor carrier enforcement. Data may not be sold or shared for other purposes.
le.retention: 9 months maximum. Exceptions for toll collection, preservation orders, and warrants.
le.data_sharing: Sharing with prosecutors and other LE agencies for authorized purposes only. Aggregate anonymized data may be shared for planning and statistics.
notable_points: Data is a public record but exempt from disclosure.
Selling captured plate data is prohibited.
Violation is a class B misdemeanor.

private.summary: Private use permitted. No ALPR-specific obligations apply.

le.summary: Officers must be certified by the Vermont Criminal Justice Council to operate ALPR. All data is stored centrally through the Vermont Intelligence Center. Access to data from the last 7 days requires documented facts showing relevance to an active investigation. Historical data beyond 6 months requires a warrant or court order.
le.retention: 18 months. Exceptions for preservation orders and warrants.
le.data_sharing: Vermont Intelligence Center transmits historical data only to LE officers with a documented legitimate purpose. Out-of-state requests permitted with the same standards. Not admissible in private civil actions.
notable_points: Annual report to legislature required by January 15, including total readers, scans submitted, requests for historical data, and associated costs.
Department of Public Safety maintains the centralized storage system for all Vermont LE agencies.

private.summary: Statute applies to law enforcement agencies only. No ALPR-specific obligations apply to private operators.

le.summary: Permitted for criminal investigations, missing or endangered persons, human trafficking, outstanding warrants, stolen vehicles, and stolen license plates. System data must be deleted within 21 days. Sharing with any state, federal, private, or commercial entity database is prohibited. An ALPR alert alone is not sufficient basis for a vehicle stop.
le.retention: 21 days for system data. 2 years for audit trail data. Data tied to an active investigation retained until final disposition including appeals.
le.data_sharing: Permitted only with: other LE agencies for authorized purposes, prosecutors and defense counsel for discovery, court orders, vendor for maintenance, and public emergency alerts. No sharing with any other state, federal, private, or commercial entity.
notable_points: Written policy required covering training, approved purposes, database update procedures, internal auditing (at least every 30 days), retention, sharing restrictions, and security.
Vendors must certify: data will not be sold or shared, systems can purge data within required timeframes, and security standards are met.
Evidence obtained in violation is not admissible by the prosecution — but may be used by the defense.
Intentional misuse or unauthorized sharing is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

meta.new_statute_note: Comprehensive new statute enacted 2025 (c. 720) — substantially replaces prior law.

private.summary: Vendors contracting with agencies are regulated directly, not just the agencies. Unauthorized data sharing can result in triple damages. Legal review is required before signing any Washington agency contract.
private.data_sharing: Vendors cannot sell, lease, or share data with non-authorized parties.

pra.notes: Yes — two tracks. Vendor violations trigger state consumer protection law: actual damages, triple damages for willful violations. Separate civil remedy also available for injured parties.

notable_points: Vendors face consumer protection liability for data sharing violations — triple damages if willful.
Immigration enforcement use is explicitly prohibited.

le.summary: Permitted for specific purposes only. Immigration enforcement is explicitly banned. Data collection near schools, houses of worship, courts, food banks, healthcare facilities, and immigration offices is prohibited.
le.retention: 21 days default. Parking: 12 hrs. Traffic studies: 30 days. Commercial vehicles: 6 months. Active investigations: duration of case.
le.data_sharing: No disclosure except court proceedings. Sharing only with other authorized Washington agencies and contracted vendors for authorized purposes.

pra.notes: Yes — injured parties can sue for damages and attorney's fees. Willful violations are a criminal offense.

notable_points: Vendors face consumer protection liability — triple damages for willful data sharing violations.
Audit trail logs cannot be searched or analyzed for investigative purposes.
